originalTitle:
The Opera Singer I was walking along Rue Charlot in the third arrondisement of Paris when I stumbled upon a Sunday morning street market.  As I turned the corner I encountered this man, surrounded by a crowd of people gathered to hear him sing Italian opera at  Le Lutétia, a sidewalk cafe.  He had an amazing voice and held his audience spellbound.  I found a table, sat down, ordered myself a glass of French wine, while I watched in awe, as people spontaneously joined in on the familiar lyrics  The crowd, presumably neighborhood friends, all gave him an overwhelming ovation, as he well deserved.  I must say that this was one of my most memorable moments in Paris.  Sometimes you just have to walk, walk and walk with no agenda because you'll never know what happy scenes you might encounter along the way.

Aulis Junes - August 16th, 1938 – September 30th 2023 There is an old, wooden house on the hill over Töölö Bay in Helsinki. It's really huge, 1200 sq. meters, three floors, attic, basement, and innumerable large rooms. I had been strolling past it for more than a decade, but had never walked in. Until today.

Each room in the house is filled with lots and lots of furnitures, books on top of each other, old dolls, flower vases, radios, music instruments, clothes, costumes, toys etc. etc. etc...

The first floor of the house has been converted into a flea market. Endless piles with different objects have been accumulated there, covered with layers of dust and time.

The other floors are incredibly beautiful with old antiques, stuff that has surely seen better days way long into the past. And yet, its beauty remains still alive in Aulis' old house.

I have to thank the gorgeous Scilla siberica on the hill which had paved my way into Aulis'.

Terry - 53 of 100 I had just gotten the kids down in bed and was relaxing on the couch when my cousin called.
"Hey man, I know its a long shot but Alien Ant Farm is in town and the cover is only five bucks."
Of course I wanted to go; I hadn't been to concert in years.
"I don't know man, let me call you back" I said.
I heard the kids up and making noises, meaning they clearly hadn't been asleep. I headed up there to calm them back down and gave the idea of the concert up, thinking, its too late now. 10 pm is pretty late when you have small children. After both kids were settled again I went down stairs to rub my wife's shoulders for a while.
"Are you going to the concert?" she asked.
I was a bit surprised, thinking, the opportunity had long passed.
"You don't care if I go?"
"As long as the kids stay down I'll head to bed myself."
"Well, if you don't care then yeah, I'm gunna go!"
I called up my cousin, got directions to the show, packed my camera and headed out.

originalTitle:
Mr. Luigi || Portrait - Eboli (SA) Italy  About this shot: 
This is another shot taken at Bar degli Amici in Eboli, my favourite hangout!
This portrait is part of a series that I intend to continue over time.
Portrait of Ordinary People, with their stories, their problems, their secrets…

 About this subject: 
Mr. Luigi is an old man who is often at the "Bar degli Amici". 
In his life, Luigi have done a lot of works: carpenter, mason, farmer...
His spirit is strong, young like a boy.
His passion for politic never died. Today he is a passionate leftist. 
Unforgettable are his soliloquies against Berlusconi.

In recent years, another passion is growing in his head: the scratch lottery.
Probably he hopes to overcome the economical crisis with a big win.
I wish it to him!

The other night I tried to steal him a few shots. 
I did it!
At first, was not very happy about this. Then... he allowed himself to photographs.
I'm very proud of this set!

originalTitle:
The Lived Experience © Leanne Boulton, All Rights Reserved

Street photography from Warwickshire, England.

Previously unpublished shot from April 2017.

Six years ago, while visiting my terminally ill father in hospital, I had time to spare between a change of buses and took my camera into the small market town for some street shooting to keep my mind from churning the pain over and over. It really was a depressing and downtrodden place and I picked up that feeling from almost every face I saw.
Street photography in a big city is certainly far less conspicuous!
